records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — [P1, confidence 100] The raw HTML bypass `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` stores and renders attacker-controlled feed/article markup without the normal sanitizer, so a compromised configured feed or embeddable page executes JavaScript in every forum visitor’s origin.
records.rationale: The diff adds `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in post.rb, bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline. TopicEmbed#import_remote pulls HTML from an external URL (ruby-readability on `open(url).read`) and creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so that markup is stored unsanitized as `cooked` and rendered (`raw post.cooked` in best.html.erb, and in the forum). This is a genuine XSS vector introduced by the diff; whether it's exploitable depends on trusting the configured feed/host, so confidence is high but not 100.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — [P1, confidence 100] `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|` drops the already-deployed `top_topics` table and all of its persisted rows whenever this historical migration is re-run, so recovery/rebuild execution silently destroys production data.
records.rationale: The diff verifiably adds `force: true` to the historical `create_table :top_topics` migration (`-    create_table :top_topics do |t|` / `+    create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`). Rails' `force: true` drops any existing table before recreating it, so re-executing this already-shipped migration (e.g., `db:migrate:redo` or a rebuild/recovery run) silently destroys all persisted top_topics rows. The mechanism is real and grounded in the diff; whether maintainers consider re-run of historical migrations a realistic path tempers severity, so confidence is moderate rather than absolute.
